Regret definitions used by banditlab

Source: R/result.R
regret_definitions.Rd

The package uses these exact definitions. Let \(\mu_a\) be the true expected reward of arm \(a\), \(\mu^* = \max_a \mu_a\), and \(A_t\) the arm selected at step \(t\).

  • Instantaneous pseudo-regret at step t: \(\Delta_{A_t} = \mu^* - \mu_{A_t}\). Recorded per decision in trajectories.

  • Cumulative pseudo-regret after T steps: \(R_T = \sum_{t=1}^{T} (\mu^* - \mu_{A_t})\). Recorded at checkpoints and, at the final step, in the summary.

  • Expected regret: the Monte Carlo mean of final cumulative pseudo-regret across replicates, reported by summary.bandit_result().

  • Optimal action share: the fraction of steps at which a selected arm attains \(\mu^*\).

  • Realised regret (comparing observed rewards against counterfactual draws from the optimal arm) is not computed in this version.

All quantities require known expected rewards. Environments that do not declare them (a bandit_custom() without expected_rewards) yield NA for every regret metric; no baseline is invented.
